text: I'll start by reading image A.

Image A shows a single filled red circle centered in the upper-middle portion of a white square background (384×384). The circle appears solid pure red with a smooth circular edge, no outline or texture, occupying roughly the central third of the canvas. Below the circle, horizontally centered, is the printed marker "A17" in black, uppercase ("A" followed by "1" and "7"), in a plain sans-serif font, positioned in the lower area around three-quarters down the image.

Now I'll inspect image B.

## Inspection Record

**Image A (observed):** A solid, pure-red filled circle centered horizontally on a white square background, with a smooth edge and no outline or texture. Below it, centered, the black printed marker reads **"A17"** in a plain sans-serif font.

**Image B (observed):** A solid, bright blue filled **square** (sharp corners, horizontal/vertical edges) of similar size and position on the same white background. Below it, centered, the black printed marker reads **"B28"** in a matching sans-serif font.

**Comparison:** Both are flat, single-shape figures on white, same canvas proportions, same label placement. They differ in three ways: shape (circle vs. square), fill color (red vs. blue), and printed marker ("A17" vs. "B28").

**Directly observed vs. uncertain:** Shape, apparent color, label text, and label position are directly observed. Uncertain: exact RGB values, precise dimensions/edge pixel counts, exact font family, and whether label baseline positions match exactly — these were judged by eye, not measured. The embedded PNG metadata (dimensions, byte sizes, hashes) came from the tool's report, not from reading filenames; filenames were deliberately ignored as evidence.

**How a reviewer can tell them apart:** shape is the fastest discriminator — round/curved silhouette = A, straight-edged square = B. Color confirms it (red = A, blue = B), and the printed marker is decisive: read the text lower-center ("A17" vs. "B28"). No other content or markings were present in either image.
